verdicts.claim: By default SQLite runs an automatic checkpoint when a COMMIT leaves the WAL at 1000 pages or more (about 4MB), or when the last connection
verdicts.evidence: wal.html 3.1: 'automatically checkpoint whenever a COMMIT occurs that causes the WAL file to be 1000 pages or more in size, or when the last database connection on a database file closes'; sec 6 'about 1000 pages (and is thus about 4MB'; SQLITE_DEFAULT_WAL_AUTOCHECKPOINT named

verdicts.claim: Automatic checkpoints and sqlite3_wal_checkpoint() are PASSIVE: they copy as many frames as possible without taking locks, never invoke the busy handler
verdicts.evidence: wal.html: 'checkpoints ... by the automatic checkpoint mechanism are PASSIVE'; c3ref: 'The busy-handler callback is never invoked in the SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_PASSIVE mode ... might leave the checkpoint unfinished'

verdicts.claim: A checkpoint does not normally truncate the WAL file (unless journal_size_limit is set). It lets SQLite overwrite the WAL from the start
verdicts.evidence: wal.html sec 6: 'The checkpoint does not normally truncate the WAL file (unless the journal_size_limit pragma is set)'; rewind condition in sec 2; Litestream: 'the file retains its high-water size on disk'

verdicts.claim: Since SQLite 3.11.0 (2016-02-15) the WAL size for a single transaction is proportional to the transaction size; for transactions over about a gigabyte
verdicts.evidence: wal.html: 'As of SQLite version 3.11.0 (2016-02-15), the WAL file for a single transaction should be proportional in size' and 'For transactions in excess of a gigabyte, WAL mode may fail with an I/O or disk-full error' (c3ref does not state it; 'two sources' tag is overstated)

verdicts.claim: sqlite3_wal_checkpoint_v2 has modes PASSIVE, FULL, RESTART, TRUNCATE (plus NOOP). FULL waits for no writer and all readers on the latest snapshot
verdicts.evidence: c3ref lists all five modes; TRUNCATE 'also truncates the log file to zero bytes just prior to a successful return'

verdicts.claim: Litestream runs PASSIVE checkpoints at 1000 pages or on a 1-minute interval, and forces a blocking TRUNCATE only past an emergency threshold (truncate-page-n, default 121,359
verdicts.evidence: Litestream: 'truncate-page-n: 121359 # Default: ~500MB', 'Attempts a PASSIVE checkpoint first, then falls back to a TRUNCATE', 'truncate-page-n: 0 ... WAL can grow unbounded'

verdicts.claim: Checkpoint starvation: if there is always at least one active reader, no checkpoint can complete and the WAL grows without bound. SQLite's mitigations
verdicts.evidence: wal.html: 'there is always at least one active reader, then no checkpoints will be able to complete and hence the WAL file will grow without bound'; 'reader gaps'; RESTART/TRUNCATE 'readers might block'

verdicts.claim: If the busy handler returns 0 while a FULL/RESTART/TRUNCATE checkpoint waits for the writer lock or readers, the call falls back to PASSIVE
verdicts.evidence: c3ref: 'proceeds from that point in the same way as SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_PASSIVE ... SQLITE_BUSY is returned'; other-process checkpoint lock: 'SQLITE_BUSY is returned. Even if there is a busy-handler configured, it will not be invoked'

verdicts.claim: A WAL-reset bug, present from 3.7.0 (2010) through 3.51.2, could mark WAL frames as checkpointed when they were not; fixed in 3.51.3 (2026-03-13), backports 3.44.6 and 3.50.7
verdicts.evidence: wal.html sec 11: '3.7.0 (2010-07-21) through 3.51.2 (2026-01-09). It is fixed in version 3.51.3 (2026-03-13) ... 3.44.6 and 3.50.7'; 'two or more database connections ... at the same instant'; 'this is not an emergency'

verdicts.claim: Disagreement: the blog reports the fix as 3.53.0 and says it tested that build
verdicts.evidence: blog: 'try out the version built against SQLite 3.53.0 (where the bug is fixed)'; it also says 'SQLite fixed this in March 2026', which matches 3.51.3, so the disagreement is weak; the blog names the build it tested, not the first fixed release

notes: All 5 sources were cache hits with text; 0 web fetches used.
No reviewer-addressed or injected instructions found in the source texts.
Claim 4 has a '(two sources)' tag, but only wal.html states it; the c3ref page does not.

Claim 4 puts the 3.11.0 proportional-size fact next to the >1GB failure caveat. wal.html also says that since 3.11.0 WAL handles large transactions as efficiently as rollback mode. The bullet is accurate but loses that context.
